The conditional probability for a labeled ordered pair with forward gap s to be consecutive is (1−s/L)^(N−2); shoelace and the N(N−1) choices give the stated integral, also for collinear samples. In the fourth distributional derivative of the periodic correlation, the adjacent vertex jumps have determinant 2 in forward order and −2 in reverse, and the opposite jumps have determinant zero. This gives +4 at a,b and −4 at L−a,L−b with coincident masses added. The correlation is odd with continuous second derivative, C′(0)=2ab, and ∫₀ᴸ C‴=0 yields C‴(0+) = −4. Its cubic spline integrates to the stated expectation with the Beta prefactor. Dividing the even polynomial F_k by 1−z² uses F_k(1)=0 and gives a strictly positive coefficient of z² already at k=5, so the mean decreases strictly in z. Substitution and the z→1 derivative give the rhombus maximum and unattained infimum; the leading fixed-shape deficit and exponential error also follow. The check gives 5/32 and 11/72 at N=3 for length ratios 1:1 and 1:2. The statement is an exact mean, not a distribution theorem; CHECK.py and its recorded bounded checks were inspected, not executed.
